To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new computational method to predict the expression pattern of a gene from a CRM, that this method is based on the quantitative analysis of CRM binding profiles of key TFs, and that the method has been successfully applied to predict the expression patterns of genes in the developing Drosophila wing disc.

(i) CRMs can be identified by their binding to specific sets of TFs; (ii) CRMs can have complex architectures that are not captured by simple TF‐binding site models; and (iii) the regulatory code can be deciphered by integrating TF binding data with gene expression data.
